title: Localization commutes with embedded-prime removal
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $M\to M'$ be the quotient supplied by [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points-affine-removal], and, for $f\in R$, let $M_f\to (M_f)'$ be the corresponding quotient for the localized module. Then $(M')_f\cong(M_f)'$.

proof.text: Let $K\subseteq M$ be the maximal submodule with nowhere-dense support in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ supplied by [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points-affine-removal], so $M'=M/K$. Localization at the powers of $f$ is exact, so $0\to K\to M\to M'\to0$ gives $0\to K_f\to M_f\to(M')_f\to0$ and a canonical isomorphism $(M')_f\cong M_f/K_f$.

source.place: Tag 02M7 (proof omitted in the source); localization of the exact sequence defining the quotient

proof.text: Characterize $K$. Since $R$ is Noetherian and the modules are finite, supports of submodules of $M$ are closed and $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ has finitely many irreducible components, with generic points the minimal primes $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$ of $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ (Tag 0052); so a submodule $N\subseteq M$ has nowhere-dense support in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ iff $N_{\mathfrak q_i}=0$ for all $i$. Hence $K\subseteq E:=\ker\bigl(M\to\prod_i M_{\mathfrak q_i}\bigr)$, and $E$ has nowhere-dense support, so maximality in [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points-affine-removal] gives $K=E$. The minimal primes of $\operatorname{Supp}(M_f)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap D(f)$ are the $\mathfrak q_i$ with $f\notin\mathfrak q_i$, and $(M_f)_{\mathfrak q_i}=M_{\mathfrak q_i}$ for those; for $f\in\mathfrak q_i$, $M_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is a finite $R_{\mathfrak q_i}$-module supported only at the closed point, hence killed by a power of $\mathfrak q_iR_{\mathfrak q_i}$, hence by a power of $f$, so $(M_{\mathfrak q_i})_f=0$. Localizing the exact sequence $0\to K\to M\to\prod_i M_{\mathfrak q_i}$ (finite product) at $f$ therefore gives $K_f=\ker\bigl(M_f\to\prod_{f\notin\mathfrak q_i}(M_f)_{\mathfrak q_i}\bigr)$, which by the same characterization applied to $M_f$ is the maximal submodule of $M_f$ with nowhere-dense support in $\operatorname{Supp}(M_f)$.

proof.text: Applying [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points-affine-removal] to the finite $R_f$-module $M_f$ over the Noetherian ring $R_f$, its quotient is $(M_f)'=M_f/K_f$ by Step 2. Combined with Step 1 this gives the canonical isomorphism $(M')_f\cong(M_f)'$.
